Ford, a big car company, used to **sing** praises for the UK government’s plan to make carmakers sell more electric vehicles (EVs) every year. Back in 2022, they even pushed for stricter **figures**, saying weaker targets would confuse customers and slow down progress. But now, Ford is part of a **group** complaining that these same rules are too tough—calling them “unworkable” after cutting 800 jobs in the UK.

Female leaders in the industry might argue this flip-flop shows how unpredictable the market has become. During the pandemic, carmakers had smooth **operations** because demand was high and borrowing money was cheap. But now, with fewer people buying EVs, the **fruit** of their earlier confidence—like pushing for aggressive targets—has turned sour, leaving them scrambling to adjust.

The whole situation highlights how quickly things can change. Companies that once cheered for strict rules are now struggling to keep up, proving that even well-planned policies can backfire if the market shifts. The lesson? What works today might not tomorrow, and singing a different tune later can leave a bitter taste.

P.P.S The car industry’s shift mirrors how even the loudest supporters can change their minds when reality bites.

Any other questions?
